question: Not shared at the level of population class, and this is the same comparison as C-180. P-20 is the same paper as P-19: the two source extracts are byte-identical (Cai et al., Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety 2024;285:117111). Both papers detect current MoCA-defined MCI from clinical and questionnaire tabular data. But P-339's population is hospitalised type 2 diabetes patients aged 40-75, and P-20's is working-age dust-exposed coal miners (inclusion age >= 18; mean 42.6 normal / 48.8 MCI). The predictors are tied to each population's defining condition (visceral adiposity index against work years, social support and anxiety).

figures.P-339: Nomogram, 95% CIs as printed: training (apparent, n = 236) 0.765 [0.705, 0.826]; random 30% validation (n = 101; 49 MCI/52 NC) 0.690 [0.588, 0.792]; optimism-corrected C-index 0.747 [0.695, 0.800].
figures.P-20: Identical to P-19. XGBoost 0.959 training / 0.795 validation / 0.913 separately recruited test; logistic 0.818 / 0.816 / 0.778; no AUC interval printed. Derived Hanley-McNeil. Test (50 MCI/301 normal): XGBoost 0.913, Q1 = 0.8399, Q2 = 0.8715, SE = 0.0280, CI [0.858, 0.968]; logistic 0.778, SE = 0.0403, CI [0.699, 0.857]. Validation (n = 388, about 66/322): XGBoost 0.795, SE = 0.0344, CI [0.728, 0.862]; logistic 0.816, SE = 0.0331, CI [0.751, 0.881].

matched_figure_check: As in C-180. No figure is reported in the other's population or on the other's predictors. The XGBoost test AUC (0.913) differs from both P-339 intervals in both directions. On the same model class, P-20's logistic test AUC 0.778 lies inside P-339's validation interval [0.588, 0.792], while 0.690 lies just below P-20's [0.699, 0.857] (one-way). The recorded gap is not dissolved by a matched figure, but it mixes an apparent training AUC with a test AUC, and most of it follows the XGBoost-against-logistic difference.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply to the compared figures (0.765, 0.913); P-20's random-forest training AUC 0.981 is an apparent training value and not a compared figure.
reason: This record duplicates C-180, since P-20 and P-19 are one paper, and it gets the same judgment. The gap is beyond uncertainty, but the AUCs describe MCI detection in different population classes (diabetic inpatients against dust-exposed coal miners), so condition 1 fails. The record's dataset_equal 'Yes' is wrong, and it cites P-339's apparent training AUC rather than its validation AUC. The pair should be counted once, with C-180.

quotes.quote: inclusion criteria were as follows: (1) age ranging from 40 to 75 years; (2) T2DM diagnosis according to the World Health Organization’s standards established in 1999
with AUC values of 0.765 (95% CI: 0.705–0.826) in the training cohort and 0.690 (95% CI 0.588–0.792) in the validation cohort (Fig. 4C, D).
Results from the test set showed that the AUC of the XGBoost model (AUC=0.913) outperformed the Logistic Regression model (AUC=0.778).
Workers exposed to dust who underwent health examinations at the Occupational Health Examination Center from May 2022 to October 2022 were selected as research subjects.
The data used in this model comes from a single coal mine. More external data may be needed to improve the model’s generalizability.
